title: Flyto2 Core guarded HTTP modules -- T1190 SSRF guard validates only the initial URL, aiohttp follows the 302 into internal space
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-67424 (GHSA-c9hr-64h3-gxpc,
CVSS 8.5 HIGH), affecting Flyto2 Core (`flyto-core`) <= 2.26.6.

Flyto2's `http.get`, `http.request`, and `http.batch` modules call
`validate_url_with_env_config()` before issuing a request -- the
project's own SSRF guard, correctly applied here unlike the modules
in the sibling advisory GHSA-pgwh-4jj4-qm8v. But the guard validates
only the URL the caller supplied, and the subsequent
`session.get(url, ...)` call carries no `allow_redirects=False`, so
aiohttp's default `allow_redirects=True` transparently follows any
redirect the response returns -- with no re-validation of the
`Location` target. An attacker hosts a public URL that 302-redirects
to an internal or cloud-metadata address; the guard passes on the
public host, aiohttp follows the redirect, and the internal response
body is returned to the caller through a module the project believed
was SSRF-protected.

Detection logic flags a Flyto2 `http.get`/`http.request`/`http.batch`
module invocation whose target URL is a public host that responds
with a 3xx redirect to a private, loopback, or cloud-metadata
address -- the exact guard-then-redirect sequence this advisory's
proof of concept demonstrates against a live instance.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (flyto-core, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact source files, line numbers, and a live
proof of concept confirming the redirect-to-loopback bypass), fixed in flyto-core 2.26.7+ (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
